I suppose I shall start from the very beginning. I grew up in Charwood. We were three brothers in our family. My father was a miner, like many in Charwood, but none of us wanted that kind of life for ourselves.

The eldest of us went to Nor City, but me and my older brother Heinkel stayed. Once I came of age, I moved to neighboring Brimhaven and began work as a forest ranger, but Heinkel stayed in Charwood, working for the Oakburn family, who were the wealthiest in Charwood.

message: Err, forget everything I just said then. You haven't heard a word from me.
Since the family ran away to Nor City, Feygard just accepted that and started dealing with the people directly. I heard they hit a new vein too. Good for them.

Soon the Noble Wars began. Brimhaven stood with Nor City, but the Oakburns refused to follow at first. Eventually they joined, but the other wealthy families held a grudge against them for it. When the troops of Nor City arrived, I worked for them as a scout, keeping note of enemy positions in the area and reporting any movements. I came close to being gravely hurt many times, but thanks to the Shadow I came out relatively unscathed through those years.
As you might have heard at the academy, those rich folk who held all the influence in our town quickly switched sides when Feygard was at our doorstep. So did my patron, and so did Heinkel's.

They feared that Feygard would punish them once the war was over, so they conceded to every demand in the hope it would bring them into Feygard's good graces. Food, even as we hungered, labor, and our meager troops as auxiliaries. Charwood had little to spare save for iron from its mine, which was beginning to be depleted. So the Oakburns sent men from their household's employ, among them my brother. I myself then had to work as a scout for the Feygardians.

As I was heading west with a group of Feygard soldiers, the main force was preparing to march east to take Brightport from the Eastern Coalition, my brother among them. I had faith the Shadow would watch over him, as it had over me in those years.

When I returned, it was a horrific sight. Much of the main square had been turned into a makeshift hospital. Rows were filled with Feygard knights I had only ever seen as mighty and prideful men. Some were missing limbs, others were beyond healing. Not even bonemeal potions could save them. I searched frantically for my brother, but I couldn't find him anywhere.

The men from Brimhaven who were sent alongside them stood as auxiliaries in the back ranks and were left relatively unscathed, save for those in Oakburn's employ. The other families conspired with a commander and arranged for the men from Charwood to be sent to the front lines, lightly armored as they were.

I asked anyone who was well enough to speak. I found one man who was a fresh recruit and had marched east alongside my brother. When the Feygardians were caught in an ambush, Heinkel was sent to reinforce the front lines instead of that young man's battalion.

He fought bravely, as I knew my brother would. But as the battle began to stabilize, something horrific happened. A horde of terrifying monsters assailed the battlefield. It wasn't an attack by Nor City; no sane person should believe that. They were something far worse than that. Those creatures targeted the weaker ones first, and Nor City lost even more than Feygard. But my brother... he was torn apart by a disfigured giant. I couldn't believe what I was hearing.

West of this cabin, built on land I received for my service in the war, was the battleground. I didn't witness the battle firsthand. My brother did, and he lost his life there. I only heard about it from those who were present.

A fate as horrible as this for my brother. The Shadow had forsaken us in those needless wars. I've long wondered whether my brother died with any regrets... Since then, I've witnessed the land west of here be poisoned by this curse before my own eyes.

Once the tired and war-weary people of Brimhaven learned of this news, it inspired a fervor that only a wounded prey animal fighting for survival could muster. Rather than the fight they expected, a portion of the Nor City soldiers themselves renounced their allegiance to their commander. A man known to us only as Vergas. message: "We passed the river and assumed a fighting position. The account of the battle goes into detail here, but I will cut my reading short and continue the lecture to better capture the historical nuance of the situation. The leader of the Eastern Coalition in this battle was Commander Vergas, but alongside him were a number of paladins of the Shadow, along with their organization's leader. I believe this might explain much of the context surrounding the battle that the firsthand accounts in the memoirs lack.

The Feygard legion stopped somewhere south of the bridge. General Ahrensbach would not have risked crossing the bridge to Brightport nor marching through the dense forest. Instead he intended to circle the ravine and take Brightport from the south, which, lacking natural fortifications, was harder to defend than Brimhaven. His plans were cut short, however, by the Eastern Coalition. They had maneuvered in such a way that the Feygardian heavy infantry faced south while the attack came from the north. In summary, a diversion, and an ambush from the forest. Though the legions of Feygard were not so weak as to fall to such tricks.

The two sides clashed, and the frontlines quickly stabilized before the Easterners could inflict too many casualties. But their plan had not been fully realized. It is in the following words that I explain it, and I truly warn you all of the things you are about to hear.

The Easterners summoned a horde of monsters to attack the Feygardians after they had barely recovered from the dirty tricks they were subjected to.
